tldr.text: A session hunts the previous session's high or low, and this trades the reversal off it. London hunts Asia; New York hunts London.
The {pb_dir_tf}-minute trend decides which way it trades, and the sweep is the trigger. One trade per session.
The order rests in the nearest untouched {pb_poi_tf}-minute gap.
First target at {exec_tp1_r} times risk with {exec_tp1_pct}% banked there; the rest runs to yesterday's or last week's level.

edge: This is the course model the SMC material calls its most-traded and most profitable play — London sweeping Asia, measured there at a profit factor near 3 with an average winner 6.8 times the risk. Our own six chart runs did NOT reproduce that: the win rate never left 16.7-20.1% against a break-even near 17.6%, and every run's profit sat in one to three trades. The gap is setup SELECTION, not trade management, and the filters that close it (order blocks as entry objects, zone quality grading, the news blackout) are NOT built. Read any number off this bot as a measurement of our version, never of the model it copies.

steps.title: Trend
steps.detail: The 15-minute swing structure decides the only side traded that day.

steps.title: Sweep
steps.detail: The new session must trade through the previous session's high or low. The level is frozen at the session open and never moves.

steps.title: Confirmation
steps.detail: Optional: the lower timeframe flips to agree, after the sweep. Ships OFF.

steps.title: Zone
steps.detail: The nearest untouched gap on the far side of price. An order rests at its near edge.

steps.title: Exit
steps.detail: Four fifths at 3.5 times risk, the rest to yesterday's or last week's level, stop to breakeven on the way.

params.name: pb_dir_tf
params.label: Direction — trend timeframe
params.desc: Which timeframe decides long or short. Only trades that way. The course uses 15. ⚠ It must be a whole multiple of the bar frame this run replays — a finer timeframe cannot be rebuilt from a coarser one, and the run REFUSES rather than quietly using the chart's.

params.name: pb_trade_ldn
params.label: Trade London (sweeps the Asian high/low)
params.desc: London hunts Asia's high and low.

params.name: pb_trade_ny
params.label: Trade New York (sweeps the London high/low)
params.desc: New York hunts London's high and low.

params.name: pb_require_conf
params.label: Require a lower-timeframe change of character
params.desc: On: after the level is taken, wait for the smaller timeframe to turn our way. Off: enter on the sweep alone, at worse prices. The course has this ON. It ships OFF because that is what the chart is trading — turn it on to compare.

params.name: pb_conf_tf
params.label: Confirmation timeframe
params.desc: The timeframe watched for a change of character. The course uses 1. It stays live even with confirmation switched off, because two other rules read it: cancel-on-an-opposite-shift and stop-to-breakeven-on-an-opposite-shift. 🔴 It MUST equal the bar frame this run replays — the confirmation is read off the replayed bars themselves, so a 1-minute confirmation needs a 1-minute replay. The run refuses by name otherwise.

params.name: pb_conf_when
params.label: When the shift must happen
params.desc: Before: wait for the turn, then leave an order sitting in the gap. At: wait for price to reach the gap, then the turn, then buy at market. ⚠ Never exercised by the parity gate — no export has run it.

params.name: exec_be_on_shift
params.label: Stop to breakeven when the confirmation timeframe shifts AGAINST the trade
params.desc: Moves the stop to the entry price as soon as the smaller timeframe turns against you. ⚠ Never fired in the gated export, so parity says nothing about it.

params.name: pb_poi_tf
params.label: Point of interest — timeframe the zone is found on
params.desc: Which timeframe the entry gap is found on. The course uses 5. Off means no gap is needed at all — you enter at market the moment the confirmation timeframe turns, with the stop behind the sweep. Off does nothing unless confirmation is required.

params.name: pb_poi_untouched
params.label: Untouched zones only
params.desc: On: skip any gap price has already traded back into. Off takes more trades at worse prices.

params.name: exec_tp1_mode
params.label: Target 1 — what the first target IS
params.desc: Fixed R puts the first target at a multiple of your risk, which is what the course does. Nearest level uses yesterday's or last week's high or low.

params.name: exec_tp1_r
params.label: First target (R)
params.desc: How many times your risk the first target sits at. 5 is the course's number; this ships at 3.5, which is what the chart is trading. Neither is measured.

params.name: exec_tp1_pct
params.label: % banked at the first target
params.desc: How much comes off at the first target. 0 = take nothing and ride it all to the second. At 80 the runner is a fifth of the position, so the second target moves the result far less than the first one does.

params.name: exec_use_tp1
params.label: Previous day's low / high is a target
params.desc: Use yesterday's high or low as a target. Rebuilt from the replayed bars on a 17:00 New York day boundary, which was measured against the chart rather than assumed.

params.name: exec_use_tp2
params.label: Previous week's low / high is a target
params.desc: Use last week's high or low as a target. ⚠ It cannot exist until a full week of bars has closed, so a run shorter than that silently has one fewer target.

params.name: exec_use_windows
params.label: Only execute inside the course's hours
params.desc: Only take trades during the hours below. Orders waiting outside them are cancelled.

params.name: exec_win_ldn
params.label: London hours (New York clock)
params.desc: New York clock. Our London session starts at 3am, so the first hour of the default 2am-5am window can never trade — that hour is the Frankfurt open, and Frankfurt is a session this strategy does not model.

params.name: exec_win_ny
params.label: New York hours (New York clock)
params.desc: New York clock. Our New York session starts at 8am, so the first hour of the default 7am-10am window can never trade. Effective window is 8am-10am.

params.name: pb_trade_longs
params.label: Trade longs
params.desc: Off means shorts only.

params.name: pb_trade_shorts
params.label: Trade shorts
params.desc: Off means longs only. ⚠ Every measured run of this strategy leaned short through a market that tripled, so this switch is the crudest form of the missing higher-timeframe trend filter.

params.name: exec_size_mode
params.label: Position sizing
params.desc: Risk % makes every trade worth the same. Fixed uses the same size whatever the stop. Use Risk % unless you are copying another script.

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: Risk % per trade
params.desc: How much of the account is lost if the stop is hit. This ships at 4, which is aggressive — drop it to 1 to read the SHAPE of the equity curve rather than its size. ⚠ With the $4 stop floor, 4% on gold at 3,500 is still 35 times the account in notional.

params.name: exec_fixed_qty
params.label: Contracts
params.desc: Fixed position size, in contracts. ⚠ The parity gate REFUSES an export taken in this mode — the chart's export carries no size column, so a run in fixed contracts cannot be checked against it.

params.name: pb_struct_len
params.label: Structure pivot length
params.desc: How the swing highs and lows are first found. Mostly affects warm-up. Leave it alone.

params.name: exec_zone_entry
params.label: Where the limit rests in the zone
params.desc: Near edge fills most often; far edge gets a better price but often misses.

params.name: exec_stop_from
params.label: Stop sits behind…
params.desc: The gap puts the stop just past the gap. The sweep puts it past the high or low the session made, so gap size stops mattering.

params.name: exec_sl_buf_tk
params.label: Stop buffer beyond the zone (ticks)
params.desc: How far past the edge the stop sits. On gold a tick is one cent, so 20 is twenty cents.

params.name: exec_cancel_bars
params.label: Cancel an unfilled limit after N bars
params.desc: 0 keeps the order until the session ends. It is always cancelled at the end of its session anyway.

params.name: exec_cancel_flip
params.label: Cancel on a direction flip or an opposite shift
params.desc: Pull a waiting order when the trend turns the other way.

params.name: exec_be_at_tp1
params.label: Stop to breakeven when the first target is reached
params.desc: Moves the stop to the entry price once the first target prints.

params.name: exec_be_buf_tk
params.label: Breakeven buffer (ticks)
params.desc: How far past the entry the breakeven stop sits, so you bank a few ticks instead of exactly nothing.

params.name: exec_tp_fallback_r
params.label: Fallback target (R) when no liquidity target is valid
params.desc: If no level works as a target, use this many times risk instead. 0 = skip the trade.

params.name: exec_min_rr
params.label: Minimum reward:risk to the first target
params.desc: A target nearer than this is treated as unusable. ⚠ Never fired in the gated export.

params.name: exec_min_stop_mode
params.label: Minimum stop distance
params.desc: Refuse a trade whose stop is too close to the entry. A tiny stop means a huge position, not small risk.
params.group: 8 · Safety filters that REFUSE a setup

params.name: exec_min_stop_val
params.label: Minimum stop floor (unit = mode above)
params.desc: The smallest stop allowed, in the unit picked above. $4 of gold, and this one IS measured: trades whose stop was under $4 averaged -1.43R instead of -1R, and every loss worse than -3R in six years came from that band. Above $4 the average loser flattens near -1.1R, so a bigger floor just costs trades.
params.group: 8 · Safety filters that REFUSE a setup

params.name: pb_poi_max_atr
params.label: Maximum distance to the zone (x ATR14)
params.desc: Refuse a gap further from price than this many average bar ranges. 0 = no limit. ⚠ Shipped at 0, so it has never fired and the parity gate says nothing about it.
params.group: 8 · Safety filters that REFUSE a setup

params.name: exec_time_stop_hrs
params.label: Time stop (hours, 0 = off)
params.desc: Close a trade open this long that has not reached its first target. 0 = off. ⚠ Shipped off, so it has never fired.
params.group: 8 · Safety filters that REFUSE a setup

params.name: tick_size
params.label: Tick size
params.desc: The instrument's smallest price move — one cent on gold. A platform fact, not a strategy choice.

params.name: qty_step
params.label: Lot step
params.desc: The venue's quantity step. A computed size is TRUNCATED down to it, never rounded — measured off every fill in the gated export. A platform fact, not a strategy choice.

params.name: initial_capital
params.label: Starting balance
params.desc: What the run starts with. Position size is a percentage of the running equity, so this sets the scale of every dollar figure and none of the R figures.

params.name: htf_trend_tf
params.label: Slower trend must agree
params.desc: 🔴 NOT IN THE PINE — no chart can produce it, so the parity gate forces it off and says so on every run. Turning it on makes this a DIFFERENT strategy from the one the chart trades, and a number off it may not be compared with a gated one. A second, slower trend read that must agree before anything trades. Every measured run of this strategy leaned short through a market that tripled; this is the direct test of whether that is the whole problem. ⚠ It must be a whole multiple of the replayed bar frame.

params.name: poi_max_age_bars
params.label: Refuse a gap older than N bars
params.desc: 🔴 NOT IN THE PINE — forced off by the parity gate. 0 = no limit. The course grades a point of interest by whether it belongs to the move that swept; an old gap price happens to be near is a different object from the one the sweep created.

params.name: poi_min_size_atr
params.label: Refuse a gap thinner than N x ATR(14)
params.desc: 🔴 NOT IN THE PINE — forced off by the parity gate. 0 = no limit. A thin gap means a thin stop, which the minimum-stop floor already refuses — this refuses it as a QUALITY judgement instead, and the two will overlap.

params.name: poi_max_size_atr
params.label: Refuse a gap fatter than N x ATR(14)
params.desc: 🔴 NOT IN THE PINE — forced off by the parity gate. 0 = no limit. A very wide gap is usually a news candle rather than an imbalance anyone will defend.

params.name: ob_confluence
params.label: Gap must sit on an order block
params.desc: 🔴 NOT IN THE PINE — forced off by the parity gate. Refuse unless the gap overlaps a live order block on its own side. Measured 2026-09-21: cut 71 trades to 10 and lost money.

params.name: news_before_min
params.label: News blackout — minutes before
params.desc: 🔴 NOT IN THE PINE — forced off by the parity gate. Stand aside this long before a high-impact USD release. The calendar only covers the dates this machine has cached; outside them the filter cannot ask and allows the trade.

params.name: news_after_min
params.label: News blackout — minutes after
params.desc: 🔴 NOT IN THE PINE — forced off by the parity gate. Stand aside this long after a high-impact USD release.
